scenes.heading: Stream Processing
scenes.narration: Stream processing computes results continuously over unbounded data, using windows and state to make sense of endless events.

scenes.heading: Core stream concepts
bullets: Windows group events into time buckets.
Event time versus processing time matters.
State keeps running aggregates across events.
scenes.narration: Windows slice an endless stream into finite buckets so you can aggregate, such as counts per minute. Distinguishing when an event happened from when it was processed is crucial for correctness. Watermarks tell the system how long to wait for stragglers, and managed state carries running totals forward across events.

scenes.heading: Tumbling vs sliding windows
scenes.narration: Tumbling windows are fixed and never overlap, so each event lands in exactly one bucket, perfect for periodic totals. Sliding windows overlap, letting an event contribute to several, which produces smooth moving metrics. Choosing between them depends on whether you want discrete periods or a rolling view.

scenes.heading: A windowed aggregation
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import window, count

counts = (events
    .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes")
    .groupBy(window("event_time", "5 minutes"))
    .agg(count("*").alias("events_per_window")))

counts.writeStream.outputMode("update").start()
scenes.narration: This counts events in five-minute tumbling windows based on event time, not arrival time. The watermark tells Spark to wait up to ten minutes for late events before finalizing a window. Update output mode emits revised counts as more data arrives, keeping results correct despite lateness.

scenes.text: Stream processing uses windows, event time, watermarks, and managed state to compute correct results continuously over unbounded data.
scenes.narration: Mastering windows and watermarks is what separates a stream job that is merely fast from one that is also correct.
